in_hebrew.name: גְרָגֹרִיָּה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם גְרָגֹרִיָּה הוא שם נשים בתיווך המאגיא. מקורו במילה גְרָג, שגם היא נמצאת בשם גֶּרֶג וגרג. השם ניתן להלנה, אמו של יוחנן המטביל, ובכך היא השם הראשון ששמו נקשר לעידן הנוצרי. השם גְרָגֹרִיָּה, הוא שם חזק המלמד שיפוט, נחישות ותכלית.

in_greek.name: Γρηγορία
in_greek.long_meaning: Η ονομασία Γρηγορία προέρχεται από το όνομα Γρηγόρης. Το όνομα Γρηγόρης είναι σύνθετο από τα δύο ελληνικά όνματα Γρηγόρης και Ωρία. Η Γρηγορία ήταν η μητέρα του Ιωάννη του Ταψίτη. Η ονομασία της Γρηγορίας συνδέεται με την ελληνική γλώσσα και την κουλτούρα της.

in_latin.name: Gregoriah
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Gregoriae, auctoris nominis Gregorius, significat virtutem fortitudinem, quae est virtus animi, qua homo potest vincere adversitates et superare difficultates. Nomen Gregoriae in ecclesia Latina erat in usu ab antiquo. Hoc nomen est nomen femininum et significat feminam fortis et virtuosa.

in_english.name: Gregoriah
in_english.meaning: a name signifying virtue and strength
in_english.long_meaning: The name Gregoriah is derived from the Greek name Gregor, meaning 'watchful' or 'alert'. It is associated with the virtue of watchfulness and being aware of one's surroundings. In Christian tradition, the name Gregoriah is linked to the concept of being vigilant and prepared for the second coming of Christ. The name is also associated with the qualities of strength, courage, and determination. In modern times, the name Gregoriah is often given to children born to parents who value these qualities.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gregoriah holds a significant place in Christian history, particularly in the Eastern Orthodox Church, as it is the name of several saints and biblical figures. Saint Gregory of Nazianzus, a notable Greek theologian, is one of the Cappadocian Fathers and considered a Doctor of the Church. St. Gregory Thaumaturgus, another early Christian saint from Cappadocia, is known for his miraculous powers. The name continues to be a popular one in the Christian community, reflecting the values of vigilance, protection, and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_significance: Gregoriah represents a steadfast commitment to spiritual growth and an assertion of one's faith in God. As the name's Greek roots suggest, it implores its bearer to stand guard and be alert to the subtle workings of the divine within themselves and the world around them. It signifies the importance of remaining watchful and mindful, constantly nurturing a deep spiritual connection and remaining steadfast in faith. The name's charisma and significance go beyond just being a name but serve as a daily reminder to stay in touch with one's spiritual foundation.

historical_references.reference: Gregoriah of Nyssa was a renowned theologian and Christian bishop of the 4th century AD. He was a younger contemporary of St. Basil the Great and St. Gregory of Nazianzus, and is known for his contributions to the development of Trinitarian doctrine.

Gregoriah of Tours was a Frankish bishop, historian, and hagiographer who lived in the 6th century AD. He is known for his 'Histories' which provide an important account of the early Merovingian Frankish kingdom in Gaul.

It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.
